status: Static editable walkthroughs; depicted controls are not connected prototypes. No external actions.
source: Assigned Formbricks #8650 review at commit 23cdac2. All approaches use access.ts; four inspection states reproduce the same exact lines 178–183.
order: Main workspace on page 01 with rationale beside it. On page 02, read each A–D row left to right: three states, then its rationale.

screens.title: Review by intended behavior
screens.caption: Select the first expectation. Its source, uncertainty, and evidence links appear before you inspect code.

screens.title: Review by intended behavior
screens.caption: Choose tenant membership. Inspect the pinned guard and attach what it supports, while keeping route coverage and execution unknown.
screens.action: Next: record evidence and open question

screens.title: Review by intended behavior
screens.caption: Attaching code updates the evidence ledger. The review keeps the unresolved behavior question visible.
screens.action: Outcome: a review grounded in an explicit expectation

screens.title: Review through counterexamples
screens.caption: Choose the ownership-check step in the proposed cross-tenant scenario. No exploit, defect, or execution result is claimed.

screens.title: Review through counterexamples
screens.caption: Inspect the same tenant-membership guard. Record the supported branch and keep missing caller coverage explicit.

screens.title: Review through counterexamples
screens.caption: The investigation ends with an inconclusive result and a precise request for evidence, not an invented bug.
screens.action: Outcome: a focused challenge with a traceable result

screens.title: Review from impact outward
screens.caption: Start with the verified layer dependency. Inspect the same ownership guard, then identify the missing operation call sites.
screens.action: Next: inspect the guard and caller-coverage gap

screens.title: Review from impact outward
screens.caption: Inspect the guard and its verified layer relationship. Operation call sites remain an explicit coverage gap.
screens.action: Next: record what this impact path covers

screens.title: Review from impact outward
screens.caption: The path ends with named coverage gaps. Review progress describes the inspected boundary rather than counting files.
screens.action: Outcome: a defensible review scope and a request for source

screens.action: Next: show an illustrative author handoff

screens.title: Review as an author handoff
screens.caption: Author-supplied statements become anchors for review. CodeRabbit proposes links; the reviewer checks those links and the claims.

screens.title: Review as an author handoff
screens.caption: The reviewer challenges the author’s account using the code. The source-linked question stays in an unsent local draft.
